title: Toronto officer has manslaughter charge downgraded in Chadd Facey death after 'Kijiji deal gone bad'
subtitle: The trial set for later this month will proceed on a charge of assault causing bodily harm.
article: Less than two weeks before trial, the manslaughter charge against an off-duty Toronto police officer laid in the death of a Brampton teen has been downgraded to assault causing bodily harm.

Crown prosecutor Sean Horgan told the court Friday that there was no longer a reasonable prospect of conviction on either the manslaughter or aggravated assault charges laid by the province's civilian police watchdog last year against Toronto Const. Calvin Au in the April 2021 death of 19-year-old Chadd Facey.
Instead, the trial set for later this month will proceed on a charge of assault causing bodily harm. The count carries a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison.
In light of the downgraded charges, Au's defence counsel asked to change from a jury trial to one in front of a judge alone.
Au remains out on bail ahead of trial and is suspended from the police service with pay, as is required by Ontario law.
Horgan provided reasons for the Crown's decision to downgrade the charges, saying he wanted the public to understand.

He said the forensic pathologist that initially concluded the cause of death as a brain bleed - but did not comment on the manner of death - left her role and the Crown's office was informed in late August that chief forensic pathologist Michael Pollanen would take over the case.

Pollanen provided his opinion to the Crown on Aug. 27, Horgan said. It stated his belief that the death may have been "natural" or the result of a spontaneous brain bleed, though he acknowledged this would be a "rare event".

Pollanen told the Crown he "would not unequivocally state that the trauma was the underlying cause of death, because he was not sure that it was" and would instead leave open the cause of death during testimony.
Because of that, Horgan said, "there is no longer a reasonable prospect of conviction" on the original charges.

The change in the charges is a "heartbreaking" disappointment to Fay Fagan, who is "still in the dark" about what led to her otherwise healthy son's sudden death hours after an alleged interaction with Au, an incident that also involved another off-duty Toronto police officer.
"I just feel like my heart just shattered, like somebody's sitting in my chest," Fagan said in an interview.
"I'm upset knowing that I might not get any justice for my son."

Last February, Ontario's Special Investigations Unit (SIU) charged Au with manslaughter and aggravated assault in an exceedingly rare case of an off-duty cop criminally charged in an alleged homicide. The development came nearly two years after Facey, a 19-year-old psychology student and aspiring hip-hop artist, died suddenly in hospital on April 26, 2021, just hours after an alleged interaction with Au in a Brampton park.

As first reported by the Star , the clash between Au and Facey was allegedly brought on by a "Kijiji deal gone bad" that went unreported for nearly four months, according to police tribunal documents for separate police misconduct charges laid in the case. The SIU began investigating the case after it was discovered Facey had an interaction with Au, an off-duty cop, in his final hours.

Facey's cause of death has not been released. A lawyer for the family has previously said they believe he experienced head trauma before his death; medical records provided to the Star showed paramedics who rushed to his home after he suddenly became confused and lethargic noted a "small hematoma" - a pooling of blood - at the centre of his forehead.
As is typical in cases where the SIU lays criminal charges against an officer, the watchdog has not detailed the evidence against Au to preserve his fair trial interests.

What's alleged happened during the incident is detailed in police tribunal documents for separate professional misconduct charges Au and his off-duty colleague, Const. Gurmakh Benning, face in connection to the incident (Benning is not criminally charged).
Those charges have not been proven at the tribunal.
"I'm upset knowing that I might not get any justice for my son."

According to the tribunal documents, the incident began when Au and Benning went to Brampton's Bellchase Trail and Highway 50 to buy an Apple watch from Facey, a meet-up the SIU said happened between about 2:30 p.m. and 3 p.m.
Then, believing the watch was fake, Au allegedly chased Facey down, took Facey to the ground, then held him down as the teen tried to get up, according to the tribunal documents.

According to Fagan, Facey returned home around 5 p.m. unwell. Medical records stated Facey didn't know his own name and had a "hematoma" on his head prior to being rushed to Brampton Civic Hospital around 5:35 p.m.
By 8:58 p.m., Facey had a seizure that eventually led to a "code blue," meaning respiratory or cardiac arrest, according to the medical documents.
He died soon after.
Fagan, who visits her son's grave most days, says she will be there each day of the trial.
"I'm going every day," she said. "I know it's going to be hard."
